subject: Future Tech
title: Transistors at the Atomic Limit
description: A fast breakdown of Transistors at the Atomic Limit for builders.

hook.text: The latest chips pack 100 billion transistors, each 3 nanometers wide—about 15 atoms across.

buildup.text: Moore's Law predicted transistor counts doubling every two years.

discovery.text: At 3 nm, quantum effects cause electrons to tunnel through barriers, creating leaks.

twist.text: Chipmakers are going 3D. Instead of shrinking laterally, they stack transistors vertically.

climax.text: TSMC and Samsung plan 2 nm chips by 2025 and 1.4 nm by 2027. Each generation redefines the meaning of 'small.'

punchline.text: When you can't go smaller, go upward. Chips are becoming skyscrapers.

quiz.question: Why can't transistors shrink indefinitely?
options: Smaller transistors generate too much heat
